title: Grading Improvements | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive
description:
The new update to Grading in CLO 2025.0 allows you to easily adjust grading in a separate input field and areas where grading has failed are highlighted. You can now see avatar names underneath the graded size and know which avatar is used for each size. This update also includes improved grading for graphics, which lets you lock your aspect ratio. 
Check out other new features here: https://www.clo3d.com/en/clo/features

Chapters: 
00:00 - Introduction
00:28 Grading Review 
01:50 Arrow Key movement in Property Editor 
03:36 Grading Distance and Offset pop out 
05:17 Avatar name in Object Browser 
06:32 Graphic Grading Aspect Ratio 

Questions? Comment below or ask in our CLO discord server: https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/7814962429977-How-can-I-join-CLO-Discord?utm_campaign=multi_item_banner_JointheOfficialCLODiscord&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=later-linkinbio

summary: ```markdown # Grading Improvements | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey everyone! My name is Phoebe, and we have some great updates for you regarding grading. So let's jump on in and have some fun while we learn. ## Overview of Grading Tools Alright, so here I've got a garment. It's all graded, and I'm ready to show you some great updates we have for grading. Before we dive in, let me quickly cover where you can find all your grading tools and how some of them work, just as a quick refresher. All of our grading tools are located in your 2D toolbar off to the side, at the very bottom. If you can't find them, look right here; it should be underneath the sewing tools. You will see little lines, and you can pop them out to access more of your tools. But just so you know, they're at the very bottom, especially if you're working on a smaller screen. ## Edit Grading Tool The first tool I want to discuss is the Edit Grading Tool. This tool allows you to edit your grading by selecting a line and adding in some grading. You can do this in multiple ways: - **Arrow Key Movement**: You can click here and use your arrow keys to control your movement. For example, if I know I'm adjusting by 0.25 every time I click out, each size will go up by 0.25. One of our nice updates is that you can also go down into your measurements and use your arrow keys to increase or decrease by one inch each. After making your adjustments, you can hit enter to apply the changes. For instance, I just changed the medium size by two. I can go back to zero and hit enter to reduce it. ## Individual Measurement Editing There is also an option to edit each size individually. The Edit Grading Each tool is located right below the Edit Curve Grading tool. This allows you to adjust each size on its own if you'd like. Additionally, the Edit Curve tool lets you select it and see all of your curve points, which you can then adjust as needed. Once you've selected the Edit Curve, you can also edit each graded size curve, allowing you to click and move each graded size curve point to change its profile. ## Grading Table Updates Another recent update is that you can use your arrow keys within the grading table. Within this table, you can show and hide options, and you can box out specific areas for a clearer format. This will help you see distance and offset more easily, making it simpler to edit your grading. The offsets are purposefully set between graded sizes, indicating the difference from small to medium, for example. You can double-click, increase, change values, and observe the offsets, which can be quite helpful. ## Avatar Integration A really nice update we've implemented involves avatars. I have small, medium, large, and extra-large avatars paired with their corresponding sizes. Now, I can see the avatar for each size directly underneath the graded size, making it easier to identify which avatar is in use for each size. ## Grading for Graphics Finally, we have some updates regarding grading for graphics. We have added the option to perform graphic grading using either percentage or unit measurements. You can now lock your aspect ratio to ensure that your graphic remains correctly proportioned. For instance, if I set the medium size to 100 and the large size to 115, the tool will immediately adjust the height and width to maintain the proper aspect ratio. You also have the option to switch back to unit measurements to ensure everything matches up with the correct sizing. ## Conclusion Those are just some of our updates to grading. We hope we've made it a lot easier for you! Thank you so much for watching. If you have any questions, please use the comment section. I will see you in the next video. Bye! ```
